title: Why the Tour de France leader wears yellow
hook: The Tour de France leader wears yellow because of the newspaper that started the race.
peek: The Tour de France was invented in 1903 by a sports newspaper looking for readers. That paper was printed on yellow pages, and in 1919 the race leader was given a jersey to match.
lede: In 1903 the French sports paper L'Auto was in a circulation battle with a rival, Le Vélo. Its editor, Henri Desgrange, backed a bold idea from a young journalist: a bicycle race all around France. The race sold papers, and L'Auto was printed on yellow paper. So when the Tour gave its leader a jersey in 1919, it was yellow.

bullets.text: The first Tour had six long stages and about 60 starters. Maurice Garin won it, and L'Auto's sales rose sharply, while Le Vélo closed soon afterwards.
The first rider known to wear the yellow jersey was Eugène Christophe, who put it on in Grenoble in July 1919. Some riders teased him that he looked like a canary.
The Belgian Philippe Thys later said he had worn a yellow jersey as early as 1913. Historians have found little to confirm this, so 1919 remains the accepted start.
L'Auto closed in 1944, and its successor, L'Équipe, still covers the race. The jersey long carried Desgrange's initials, HD, in his honour.
